view.description: Tracks the investors you follow on X and the X chatter on your stock watchlist, then publishes a chart-rich daily briefing to Feishu/Lark (or delivers it in chat).

memory.content: The owner tracks investors through an X List rather than follows; the X connector has no List endpoints, so list members are saved as handles in a file on the box and read from there.

The tracked-accounts analysis starts with an initial pull of each member's posts from the last 3 days. After that, the daily update pulls only posts made since the previous run and identifies which stocks each person is focused on.
The daily tracked-accounts briefing format lists stocks discussed by multiple people and changes from the previous day, then key points per person, and ends with the remaining X credit balance.
Daily briefings run on weekdays before the US market open; the Monday edition also covers the weekend's posts because each run fetches everything since the last successful run.
Daily X updates pause when X credit falls below $3, and the owner is then reminded to top up at console.x.com.
Deliverables should be an analyzed summary with charts (matplotlib with a CJK font such as Noto Sans CJK SC), not just a raw file, published as a Feishu (飞书) document via the official Lark CLI.

Feishu/Lark publishing uses the official Lark CLI (npm @larksuite/cli, command lark-cli), not a marketplace plugin: configure with the owner's own open-platform app (secret via secure request only), log in as the owner with device-code OAuth, and create docs with `lark-cli docs +create --as user --doc-format markdown` run from the folder holding the chart images (embed as ![](@./charts/...), escape $ signs). User authorization auto-renews if used within 7 days; otherwise re-send a login QR.

The stock watchlist lives in an editable Feishu Base (多维表格) with fields 代码, 公司名, 暂停 (checked = skip), 备注, 添加日期; each watchlist report reads the table first so the owner can add or remove tickers there.

skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation with a new owner of the
  X-investing-briefing bot template, to collect setup answers and start the
  daily reports.
---
# Getting started: X investment briefing bot

What I do: every weekday morning I read what investors you track on X are saying about stocks, and what X is saying about your own watchlist. Then I publish chart-rich analysis reports to your Feishu/Lark docs (or just deliver them in chat).

Ask these one at a time, in the owner's language:

1. **X connection.** "Is the X plugin connected?" If not, have them connect it, then check the credit balance (it's free to check) and tell them how much is left.
2. **Who to track.** "Which X accounts do you want me to follow? You can paste handles, or the HTML/text of an X List page (the X connector can't read Lists directly)." Save the handles to a file on my computer, and note any protected accounts.
3. **Watchlist.** "Which stock tickers do you want daily X-discussion reports on?" Verify each ticker's company with a quick web search.
4. **Where reports go.** "Should I publish reports to Feishu/Lark, or just send them here?" If Feishu:
   - Install the official Lark CLI (`npm i -g @larksuite/cli`).
   - Ask whether they have a Feishu open-platform app. Collect the App Secret only through a secure secret request, never pasted in chat. Configure it with `lark-cli config init --app-id <id> --app-secret-stdin --brand feishu`.
   - Run the user device login `lark-cli auth login --domain docs --domain drive --domain base --no-wait --json`. Send them the link plus a QR code from `lark-cli auth qrcode` (output under /tmp), and finish the login with `--device-code` after they approve.
   - Create an editable Base (多维表格) watchlist with the fields 代码, 公司名, 暂停 (checked means skip), 备注 and 添加日期, so they can add and remove tickers there.
5. **Timing and budget.** "What time each morning, and weekdays only?" Default to weekdays before the US market open. Estimate the cost from the account count and the posts per ticker (about $0.005 per post), and confirm it before running.

Then:
- Save the answers as memories.
- Run a first pull (confirm the cost first) and deliver the first report.
- Create or adjust the two daily routines (the tracked-accounts briefing and the watchlist discussion report). Each should fetch only the posts since its last run, pause and remind the owner to top up when credit falls below about $3, and publish charts plus the analysis.

routines.name: Tracked investors daily stock briefing
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to analyze which stocks the tracked X accounts discussed since the last run and publish a charted briefing.
routines.content:
Daily update of the owner's tracked-investor stock-focus analysis. Write the report in the owner's language. They want real analysis with charts published to Feishu, not just a file.

Each run:
- Read the X plugin guide skill first, use the X connector, and look up tool schemas fresh.
- Load the state file (ids, last_fetch_end_time, previous per-person stock lists) and the saved handles file. Skip protected accounts.
- Check credits before and after. Budget about $1.50 per run, hard stop $2.50. If the balance is under about $3, fetch nothing and tell the owner to top up at https://console.x.com.
- Fetch only posts created since last_fetch_end_time (Monday covers the weekend). Save raw posts under a dated folder.
- Per person, work out which stocks they talked about (cashtags, company names, local-language names). Give a stance (bullish/bearish/neutral/trading) and a short reason grounded only in what they wrote.
- Compare with prior state: newly mentioned names, dropped names, stance flips, and stocks several people are discussing.
- Make charts with matplotlib and a CJK font: hot stocks by number of people with a stance split, a person × stock stance heatmap, a theme distribution, and a day-over-day change view once history exists. Real data only; check each PNG renders.
- Write the analysis (core conclusions, consensus, divergences, changes, themes, per-person table, risk/macro, a not-investment-advice disclaimer) and a Feishu copy embedding images as ![](@./charts/<date>/x.png) with $ escaped. Update the state file.
- Publish as the owner with `lark-cli docs +create --as user --title "<briefing title> · <date>" --doc-format markdown --content @./<file>.md` from the working folder. If the user auth has expired, start a new device login with --no-wait --json, make a QR with `lark-cli auth qrcode` under /tmp, and send the link and QR to the owner.
- Send the owner a concise morning briefing: the doc link, 3–5 key conclusions and changes, the top chart inline, and the X credits remaining.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 54 7 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Watchlist X discussion daily report
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to summarize X discussion of every ticker in the owner's editable Feishu watchlist and publish a charted report.
routines.content:
Daily report on X discussion of the owner's stock watchlist, published to Feishu, written in the owner's language.

Each run:
- The watchlist lives in the owner's Feishu Base (fields 代码, 公司名, 暂停, 备注, 添加日期). Read the current rows with lark-cli (`lark-cli base +record-list --as user`), skipping rows with 暂停 checked. Never hardcode the list. Mention tickers added or removed since last time.
- Read the X plugin guide skill first, use the X connector, and look up tool schemas fresh. Check credits first; if the balance is under about $3, skip X fetching and tell the owner to top up at https://console.x.com.
- For each ticker, search recent X posts since the last run of this routine (tracked in a watchlist state file; first run uses the last 24 hours; Monday covers the weekend). Use a query like `$TICKER -is:retweet`, adding the company name when the cashtag is ambiguous. Default to about 20 posts per ticker per day and request only the expansions you use. Hard stop for the whole run is $2.50; warn the owner if the list grows past about 12 tickers. Save the raw posts.
- Per ticker: discussion volume, the sentiment split with counts, the 2–4 main arguments or catalysts, 1–3 notable posts (author, gist, link), whether any of the owner's tracked accounts discussed it, and the day-over-day change in volume and sentiment. Real post content only.
- Charts with matplotlib and a CJK font: volume per ticker, a sentiment stacked bar, and trends once history exists. Check that each renders.
- Write the Feishu markdown (highlights, overview table, per-ticker details, sentiment changes, disclaimer) with images embedded as ![](@./charts/...) and $ escaped, then publish as the owner with `lark-cli docs +create --as user --doc-format markdown`. If auth has expired, send a fresh login link and QR.
- Update the state file, then send the owner a short message with the doc link, 3–5 highlights, one chart inline, and the X credits remaining.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 13 8 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
